rule: Mark column headers with <th> and scope="col" so screen readers announce the column when navigating table cells.
quote: If I use my screen reader to navigate to a row cell, it will read out the header under which it sits, letting me know which column I am currently in.

rule: Use scope="row" on row headers to clarify that a header labels cells to its right, not below.
quote: Unless you state it explicitly, it isn't clear whether a header labels cells below it or to its right. That's where the scope attribute comes in.

rule: Style spacing context, not individual elements; use adjacent sibling combinator to inject margin only between elements.
quote: margin is really a property of the relationship between two proximate elements

rule: Base vertical spacing on body text line-height to align spacing rhythm with typographic rhythm.
quote: The vertical spacing of your design should be based on your standard line-height because text dominates most pages

rule: Use CSS custom properties for exception-based spacing overrides within layout contexts.
quote: you can create per-element exceptions within a single Stack context (i.e. at the same nesting level)

rule: Use content-aware media queries, not device-based breakpoints, to reconfigure layout when content requires it.
quote: It's important we use content rather than device based @media queries. That is, we should intervene anywhere the content needs reconfiguration

rule: Use flex-basis to suggest ideal element width rather than width to enforce fixed dimensions regardless of context.
quote: flex-basis: 20rem is more nuanced. It tells the browser to consider 20rem as an ideal or target width

rule: Think intrinsically about element dimensions and let the browser generate breakpoints based on available space, not viewport width.
quote: Instead of manually pairing the column count to the viewport width, I'm telling the browser to generate the columns based on my desired column width

rule: Limit visible options to avoid overwhelming users and degrading decision quality.
quote: Too many options hurts users' decision-making ability.

rule: Enable side-by-side comparison when users must choose between related options or pricing tiers.
quote: avoid choice overload by enabling side-by-side comparison of related items and options that require a decision

rule: Prioritize featured content and add search or filtering tools to narrow choices upfront.
quote: prioritizing the content that's shown to them at any given moment (e.g. featured product), providing tools for narrowing down choices up front (e.g. search and filtering)

rule: Group content into visually distinct chunks with clear hierarchy so users scan and process faster.
quote: Structuring content into visually distinct groups with a clear hierarchy enables designers to align information with how people evaluate and process digital content.

rule: Use separate visual rules and distinctive modules to show content relationships and underlying structure.
quote: grouping content into distinctive modules, applying rules to separate content, and providing hierarchy

rule: Reduce intrinsic cognitive load by helping users absorb information and track goals without extra effort.
quote: Intrinsic cognitive load refers to the effort required by users to carry around information relevant to their goal, absorb new information and keep track of their goals.

rule: Remove distracting and unnecessary design elements that consume mental resources without aiding comprehension.
quote: Extraneous cognitive load refers to the mental processing that takes up resources but doesn't help users understand the content

rule: Provide system feedback within 400 milliseconds to maintain user attention and productivity.
quote: Provide system feedback within 400 ms in order to keep users' attention and increase productivity.
finding: 400 milliseconds threshold for system response time

rule: Use animation to engage users visually during loading or background processing.
quote: Animation is one way to visually engage people while loading or processing is happening in the background.

rule: Show progress bars to make wait times tolerable, regardless of their measured accuracy.
quote: Progress bars help make wait times tolerable, regardless of their accuracy.

rule: Add intentional delay to increase perceived value and user trust, even if the process runs faster.
quote: Purposefully adding a delay to a process can actually increase its perceived value and instill a sense of trust

rule: Make touch targets large enough for accurate selection and easy acquisition.
quote: Touch targets should be large enough for users to accurately select them.

rule: Space touch targets far apart to prevent accidental selection of adjacent controls.
quote: Touch targets should have ample spacing between them.

rule: Place task-related buttons close to users' focus area to minimize distance and interaction time.
quote: the distance between a user's task/attention area and the task-related button should be kept as short as possible

rule: Balance task difficulty with user skill level to sustain focused engagement and prevent frustration or boredom.
quote: Flow occurs when there is a balance between the difficulty of a task with the level of skill at the given task.

rule: Provide immediate feedback so users know what action was performed and what has been accomplished.
quote: Design for flow by providing the necessary feedback so that the user know what action has been done and what has been accomplished.

rule: Remove unnecessary friction and surface content and features for discovery to maintain user engagement.
quote: Optimize for efficiency and system responsiveness by removing any unnecessary friction, and making content and features available for discovery to avoid disengagement with the interface.

rule: Show clear progress indication to motivate users toward task completion.
quote: Provide a clear indication of progress in order to motivate users to complete tasks.

rule: Provide artificial progress markers to sustain motivation and task completion rates.
quote: Providing artificial progress towards a goal will help to ensure users are more likely to have the motivation to complete that task.

rule: Minimize choices at critical decision points to reduce decision time and enable faster response.
quote: Minimize choices when response times are critical to decrease decision time.

rule: Break complex tasks into smaller sequential steps to reduce cognitive load.
quote: Break complex tasks into smaller steps in order to decrease cognitive load.

rule: Highlight recommended options to prevent user overwhelm when multiple choices exist.
quote: Avoid overwhelming users by highlighting recommended options.

rule: Introduce features progressively during onboarding to minimize cognitive load for new users.
quote: Use progressive onboarding to minimize cognitive load for new users.

rule: Align interface patterns with familiar mental models users have formed from other products.
quote: By leveraging existing mental models, we can create superior user experiences in which the users can focus on their tasks rather than on learning new models.

rule: Allow users to preview and revert to familiar designs when introducing significant changes.
quote: When making changes, minimize discord by empowering users to continue using a familiar version for a limited time.

rule: Use borders or backgrounds to define clear boundaries that group related elements together.
quote: Common region creates a clear structure and helps users quickly and effectively understand the relationship between elements and sections.

rule: Position related elements close together to establish perceived relationships and shared functionality.
quote: Proximity helps to establish a relationship with nearby objects. Elements in close proximity are perceived to share similar functionality or traits.

rule: Prevent visual overwhelm by organizing information into simple, ordered patterns.
quote: The human eye likes to find simplicity and order in complex shapes because it prevents us from becoming overwhelmed with information

rule: Use color, shape, size, and orientation to signal that elements share meaning or function.
quote: Color, shape, and size, orientation and movement can signal that elements belong to the same group and likely share a common meaning or functionality

rule: Differentiate links and navigation visually from normal text to avoid ambiguity.
quote: Ensure that links and navigation systems are visually differentiated from normal text elements

rule: Perceive separated elements as a group when they share visual properties like color or shape.
quote: The human eye tends to perceive similar elements as a complete picture, shape, or group, even if those elements are separated

rule: Connect related functions visually via colors, lines, frames, or shapes to show relationships.
quote: Group functions of a similar nature so they are visually connected via colors, lines, frames, or other shapes

rule: Use tangible connectors like lines or arrows between elements to establish visual relationships.
quote: you can use a tangible connecting reference (line, arrow, etc) from one element to the next to also create a visual connection

rule: Match product design to users' existing mental models to enable knowledge transfer.
quote: Match designs to the users' mental models to improve their experience. This enables them to easily transfer their knowledge from one product or experience to another

rule: Use familiar patterns and conventions in e-commerce to conform to user expectations.
quote: e-commerce websites, which use consistent patterns and conventions such product cards, virtual carts and checkout flows in order to conform to users' expectations

rule: Conduct user research to align your design with users' mental models of how systems work.
quote: The task of shrinking the gap between our own mental models and those of the users is one of the biggest challenges we face, and to achieve this goal we use a variety of user research methods

rule: Chunk content into smaller units to help users process, understand, and memorize information.
quote: Organize content into smaller chunks to help users process, understand, and memorize easily

rule: Account for working memory limits that vary by individual knowledge and situational context.
quote: short-term memory capacity will vary per individual, based on their prior knowledge and situational context

rule: Remove elements that don't compromise function to reduce overall complexity.
quote: Analyze each element and remove as many as possible, without compromising the overall function

rule: Avoid complexity at the outset rather than trying to reduce it later.
quote: The best method for reducing complexity is to avoid it in the first place

rule: Provide contextual guidance throughout the product, not upfront documentation, so users can learn while accomplishing immediate tasks.
quote: Make guidance accessible throughout the product experience and design it to fit within the context of use

rule: Prioritize design effort on the 20% of features and flows that deliver 80% of user value and impact.
quote: Focus the majority of effort on the areas that will bring the largest benefits to the most users

rule: Set and display expected task duration to prevent users from expanding effort to fill available time.
quote: Limit the time it takes to complete a task to what users expect it'll take

rule: Use autofill and pre-populated fields in forms to reduce actual task completion time below user expectations.
quote: Leverage features such as autofill to save the user time when providing critical information within forms

rule: Design the most intense moments and the final moments of a user journey to create lasting positive impressions.
quote: Pay close attention to the most intense points and the final moments (the "end") of the user journey

rule: Soften negative experiences with character, illustration, animation, or humor to prevent lasting negative impressions.
quote: infusing a touch of brand character through illustration, subtle animation, and humor, the tool defuses what could potentially be a stressful moment

rule: Accept variable and non-standard user input, translating it to meet your system's requirements while providing clear feedback.
quote: Accept variable input from users, translating that input to meet your requirements, defining boundaries for input, and providing clear feedback

rule: Anticipate diverse user capabilities and access patterns, building resilience into design through flexible and tolerant interfaces.
quote: Be empathetic to, flexible about, and tolerant of any of the various actions the user could take or any input they might provide

rule: Avoid styling content to resemble ads or placing it near ads, as users consciously ignore banner-like information.
quote: Users have learned to ignore content that resembles ads, is close to ads, or appears in locations traditionally dedicated to ads

rule: Guide user attention to relevant information and actions by reducing visual clutter and distracting competing changes.
quote: Designers must guide users' attention, prevent them from being overwhelmed or distracted, and help them find relevant information or action

rule: Analyze designs for simultaneous competing visual changes that divert attention; avoid triggering change blindness.
quote: Avoid this by analyzing your design for any competing changes that may happen at the same time and that may divert attention from each other

rule: Use consistent sequences, terminology, colors, layout, fonts, and capitalization throughout interfaces.
quote: Consistent sequences of actions should be required in similar situations; identical terminology should be used in prompts, menus, and help screens; and consistent color, layout, capitalization, fonts, and so on, should be employed throughout.

rule: Design interfaces to serve users across novice-to-expert ranges, ages, disabilities, and international contexts.
quote: Recognize the needs of diverse users and design for plasticity, facilitating transformation of content. Novice to expert differences, age ranges, disabilities, international variations, and technological diversity each enrich the spectrum of requirements that guides design.

rule: Provide interface feedback for every user action, scaled to the significance of that action.
quote: For every user action, there should be an interface feedback. For frequent and minor actions, the response can be modest, whereas for infrequent and major actions, the response should be more substantial.

rule: Organize action sequences into grouped tasks with a clear beginning, middle, and end plus completion feedback.
quote: Sequences of actions should be organized into groups with a beginning, middle, and end. Informative feedback at the completion of a group of actions gives users the satisfaction of accomplishment, a sense of relief, a signal to drop contingency plans from their minds, and an indicator to prepare for the next group of actions.

rule: Ensure visual design improvements do not harm productivity, learnability, or satisfaction through user testing.
quote: User test after aesthetic changes have been made, benchmarking, where applicable, the new design against the old. Ensure that learnability, satisfaction, and productivity have been improved or at least have stayed the same.

rule: Apply aesthetically pleasing design; it creates positive perception and increases perceived usability.
quote: An aesthetically pleasing design creates a positive response in people's brains and leads them to believe the design actually works better.
finding: Users with aesthetically pleasing design showed stronger correlation between aesthetic appeal and perceived ease of use than actual ease of use (Kurosu & Kashimura, 1995, n=252).

rule: Beware: attractive design can mask usability problems and prevent issues from being discovered in testing.
quote: Visually pleasing design can mask usability problems and prevent issues from being discovered during usability testing.

rule: Show affordance that content is slidable: use a focus style and ensure the rightmost item is partially cut off.
quote: There are already a couple of things that tell the user this is a slidable region: the focus style, and the fact that the right-most image is usually cut off, suggesting there is more to see.

rule: Hide collapsed content with the hidden attribute so it is not focusable by keyboard users.
quote: Another advantage is that keyboard users do not have to step through all of the focusable elements on the page to get to where they want to go: Hidden content is not focusable.

rule: Do not use tabbed interfaces for site-wide navigation; tabs expect within-page behavior, not page navigation.
quote: It is for the same reason that a tabbed design should not be employed for site-wide navigation. At the very least, when a user selects a "tab" they would not expect to be navigated to an entirely new page!

rule: Use semantic HTML (table of contents + same-page links) before adding ARIA tab semantics.
quote: For my money, an embryonic tabbed interface is just a table of content with same-page links pointing at different sections of the page.

rule: Implement dark mode by augmenting existing styles, not loading separate stylesheets.
quote: The most efficient course of action is not to provide a completely alternative stylesheet, but to augment the existing styles directly, as tersely as possible.

rule: Use aria-labelledby for primary tooltip labels and aria-describedby for supplementary tooltips.
quote: A notifications control with a tooltip reading "Notifications" treats the tooltip as a primary label. Alternatively, a tooltip that reads "View notifications and manage settings" is supplementary.

rule: Make tooltips visible on keyboard focus, not only on hover, so keyboard users can access them.
quote: The tooltip text is available on focus, just as it would be on hover for sighted users.

rule: Hide delete buttons on hover and show them permanently, or provide keyboard access; do not hide functionality from keyboard users.
quote: Most notably, the delete functionality only appears on hover, making it an entirely inaccessible feature by keyboard.

rule: Place key actions on the far left and right of navigation elements to increase memorization.
quote: Positioning key actions on the far left and right within elements such as navigation can increase memorization.

rule: Place least important items in the middle of lists because they are stored less in working and long-term memory.
quote: Placing the least important items in the middle of lists can be helpful because these items tend to be stored less frequently in long-term and working memory.

rule: Shift core complexity from the user to the system during design and development.
quote: All processes have a core of complexity that cannot be designed away and therefore must be assumed by either the system or the user.

rule: Make guidance accessible and contextual so new users can find help regardless of their path.
quote: Make guidance accessible and fit within the context of use so that it can help these active new users, no matter what path they choose to take (e.g., tooltips with helpful information).

rule: Make important information or key actions visually distinctive.
quote: Make important information or key actions visually distinctive.

rule: Use restraint when emphasizing visual elements to prevent them competing and appearing as ads.
quote: Use restraint when placing emphasis on visual elements to avoid them competing with one another and to ensure salient items don't get mistakenly identified as ads.

rule: Do not rely exclusively on color to communicate contrast to users with color vision deficiency.
quote: Don't exclude those with a color vision deficiency or low vision by relying exclusively on color to communicate contrast.

rule: Carefully consider users with motion sensitivity when using motion to communicate contrast.
quote: Carefully consider users with motion sensitivity when using motion to communicate contrast.

rule: Display only necessary and relevant information since working memory holds 4-7 chunks for 20-30 seconds.
quote: Working memory is limited to 4-7 chunks of information at any given moment with each chunk fades after 20-30 seconds.

rule: Support recognition over recall by visually differentiating visited links and providing breadcrumbs.
quote: We can support recognition over recall by making it clear what information has already been viewed (e.g. visually differentiating visited links and providing breadcrumbs links).

rule: Provide clear signifiers of additional content to invite discovery.
quote: Invite content discovery by providing clear signifiers of additional content.

rule: Provide artificial progress toward a goal to motivate users to complete tasks.
quote: Providing artificial progress towards a goal will help to ensure users are more likely to have the motivation to complete that task.

rule: Provide clear progress indication to motivate users to complete tasks.
quote: Provide a clear indication of progress in order to motivate users to complete tasks.

rule: Keep users informed of system status through appropriate feedback within reasonable time.
quote: The design should always keep users informed about what is going on, through appropriate feedback within a reasonable amount of time.

rule: Present feedback to the user as quickly as possible, ideally immediately.
quote: Present feedback to the user as quickly as possible (ideally, immediately).

rule: Use words and concepts familiar to users rather than internal jargon.
quote: The design should speak the users' language. Use words, phrases, and concepts familiar to the user, rather than internal jargon.

rule: Follow real-world conventions and present information in natural, logical order.
quote: Follow real-world conventions, making information appear in a natural and logical order.

rule: Make controls follow real-world conventions for natural mapping to ease learning.
quote: When a design's controls follow real-world conventions and correspond to desired outcomes (called natural mapping ), it's easier for users to learn and remember how the interface works.

rule: Provide a clearly marked emergency exit to leave unwanted actions without extended process.
quote: Users often perform actions by mistake. They need a clearly marked "emergency exit" to leave the unwanted action without having to go through an extended process.

rule: Support Undo and Redo to give users control and confidence.
quote: Support Undo and Redo .

rule: Follow platform and industry conventions to meet user expectations.
quote: Users should not have to wonder whether different words, situations, or actions mean the same thing. Follow platform and industry conventions.

rule: Maintain internal consistency across a product and external consistency with industry standards.
quote: Improve learnability by maintaining both types of consistency: internal and external.

rule: Prevent errors by eliminating error-prone conditions or confirming actions before commit.
quote: Good error messages are important, but the best designs carefully prevent problems from occurring in the first place. Either eliminate error-prone conditions, or check for them and present users with a confirmation option before they commit to the action.

rule: Avoid slips by providing helpful constraints and good defaults.
quote: Avoid slips by providing helpful constraints and good defaults .
